IS:11301-1985

Indian Standard
METHODS FOR DETERMINATION OF PHOSALONE RESIDUES IN FOOD COMMODITIES
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 24 June 1985, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides Residues Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 Phosalone formulations are used in agriculture for the control of many insect pests. Frequent and increased use of these formulations often result in harmful effects due to toxic nature of residues. Careful monitoring of residues, is therefore, an important step in safeguarding human health and in formulation of regulatory policy. 0.3 In the preparation of this standard due consideration has been given to the limits likely to be laid down under the provisions of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules and the specified test methods are sensitive to the levels indicated in 1.1.1. 0.4 This standard will enable the health authorities and other engaged in the field to follow a uniform test procedure fOT the estimation of phosalone residues in various foods. 0.5 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960*.

1. SCOPE
alkali flame-ionization detector ( AFID ), and electron capture detector ( ECD ) for t h e d e t e r m i n a t i o n o f p h o s a l o n e [ 0, O-diethyl-S( 6-chlorobenzoxazolone+yl )-methyl phosphorodithioate ] residues in food commodities.

1.1.1 The minimum limit of determination of phosalone residues using alkali flame-ionization detector is 0.1 `Lg!g while it is 0'05 pg/g with electron capture detector. 2. Q U A L I T Y O F R E A G E N T S
2.1 Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled water ( see IS : 1070-1977* ) shall be employed in tests.
N OTE -- `Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities which affect the result of analysis,

3. SAMPLING 3.1 Representative samples of the material for estimating phosalone residues shall be drawn in accordance with IS : 11380 (Part 1 )-19857. 4. EXTRACTION

4.1 Reagents
4.1.1 Solvents - Acetone, acetonitrile, petroleum ether, n-hexane and dichloromethane. All glass distiIIed. 4.1.2 Sodium Chloride 4.1.3 Sodium Sulfihate - Anhydrous. 4.1.4 Glass Wool - Rinse with acetone and methanol several times and dry before use. 4.1.5 Adsorbent for Column Chromatograplv - Florisil ( 60 to 160 mesh ). 4.2 Apparatus 4.2.1 High Speed Blender - Warin g or equivalent with glass jar, teflon washers and seals. 4.2.2 Centrftfge - Capable of 3 000 r/min and having proper capacity centrifuge bottles. 4.2.3 K u d e r n a - D a n i s h C o n c e n t r a t o r - H a v i n g 500-ml flask and 10 to l&ml receiving tube with Snyder column. 4.2.4 Rotary Vacuum Evaporator .-__

*Specification for Cvater for general laboratory use ( second rcuision ). tMethods of sampling for the determination of pesticic!e residues: Part I Agricultural and food commodities. 4

IS : 11301 - 1985 4.2.5 Separating Funnel - one-litre capacity. 4.2.6 Chromatographic Tube - 2.2 cm outer diameter and 40 cm long with stop-cock.
4.3 Non-fatty Foods ( Less Than 2 Percent Fat Content )

4.3.1 Vegetables and Fruits ( Containing More Than 75 Percent Moisture ) Transfer 50 g of the sample to a Waring blender with 100 ml acetone and blend for 2 minutes at high speed. Filter extract through pre-washed glass wool plug held on a conical funnel into a beaker. Re-extract the residual sample material with two 50 ml portions of acetone by blending for 2 minutes each and filter through the same glass wool p l u g . Concentrate the combined extract to about 100 ml in a rotary vacuum evaporator. Transfer it to a 1-litre separating funnel, containing 100 ml petroleum ether and 100 ml of dichloromethane. Shake for 1 minute, allow the layers to separate. Transfer the lower aqueous layer into another l-litre separating funnel. Dry the retained upper organic layer of the first separating funnel by passing through 4 cm thick anhydrous sodium sulphate supported on glass wool in a funnel and collect in a Kuderna-Danish concentrator or rotary vacuum evaporator flask. To the separating funnel containing the aqueous phase, add 5 g sodium chloride and shake for half-a-minute to dissolve the salt. Add 100 ml dichloromethane, shake for one minute and allow the phases to separate. Collect the lower organic phase into the Kuderna-Danish concentrator after passing it through the same anhydrous sodium sulphate plug. Repeat partitioning wit 11 one more portion of 100 ml of dichloromethane. Rinse the sodium sulphate plug with 50 ml of dichloromethane into the concentrator. Discard the aqueous fraction. Evaporate the combined partitioned organic extract in a Kuderna-Danish concentrator/rotary vacuum evaporator to suitable volume. Ensure complete removal of dichloromethane by repeated evaporation with the addition of 20 ml acetone. Concentrate to about 2 ml.
4.3.2 Cereals and Pukes ( Containing Less Than 20 Percent Moisture ) W e i g h 20,O g of the sample into the blender jar and add 150 ml of 35 percent water in acetone ( 350 ml distilled water diluted to 1 litre with acetone ). Blend at high speed for 2 minutes and filter under pressure through pre-washed Whatman filter paper No. 1 placed on a Buchner funnel. Re-extract the residual material with two 50 ml portions of 35 percent water-acetone by blending for 2 minutes and filter under pressure quickly. Concentrate the combined filtrate to about 100 ml in a rotary vacuum evaporator/Kuderna-Danish concentrator and t r a n s f e r t o a I-litre s e p a r a t i n g f u n n e l c o n t a i n i n g 1 0 0 m l o f Partition and dichloromethane and 100 ml of petroleum ether. concentrate to volume as in 4.3.1. 5

IS :11301-1985 4.3.3 Water and Beverages - Partition twice 500 ml portion of I-litre sample having 7 g sodium chloride dissolved in it with 100 ml of dichloromethane in a separating funnel. Collect the lower dichloromethane layer through a plug of anhydrous sodium sulphate and concentrate as described in 4.3.1. 4.4 Fatty Foods ( Containing More Than 2 Percent Fat ) 4.4.1 Rats and Oils - Completely dissolve 5 g sample in about 150 ml of n-hexane and transfer to a separating funnel. Partition thrice with 100, 50, 50 ml of acetonitrile. Each time collecting the lower acetonitrile layer into the second separating funnel, containing 600 ml of 2 percent sodium ch!oride solution in distilled water. T o t h i s , add 100 ml of petroleum ether and shake thoroughly for 1 minute and allow layers to separate. Drain the lower aqueous phase into another separating funnel and repeat partitioning twice more. Combine the upper petroleum ether layer by passing over a plug of anhydrous sodium sulphate and concentrate in a rotary vacuum evaporator/Kuderna-Danish concentrator to about 5 ml. 4.4.2 Oilsceds and Nuts-Transfer 50-O g of crushed sample with 10 g anhydrous sodium sulphate into a blender jar. Add 150 ml of acetone and blend at high speed for 3 minutes. Filter under pressure through a pre-washed Whatman No. 1 filter paper placed over a Buchner funnel. Re-extract the residual material twice more with 75 ml portion of acetone. Evaporate the combined filterate to almost oily layer in a Kuderna-Danish-Concentrator/rotary vacuum evaporator. Dissolve oily residue in 100 ml of n-hexane and partition with acetonitrile as in 4.4.1. 4.4.3 Meat and Fish - Transfer 50.0 g of the minced sample with 20 g o f a n h y d r o u s soJium s u l p h a t e in a blender .jar. A d d 1 5 0 m l o f n - h e x a n e - k e t o n e ( 2 : 1 v/u) and blend for 3 minutes at high s p e e d . Filter under pressure through prewashed Whatman filter paper No. 1 placed on a Buchner funnel. Re-extract the residual material twice with 100 ml portion of n-hexane-acetone and follow concentration and partitioning as given in 4.4.1. 4.4.4 Milk and Milk Products -Transfer 100 g milk in the blender jar. Add 10 g of anhydrous sodium sulphate and 100 ml of acetone and blend for 2 minutes. Filter under pressure through prewashed Whatman filter paper No. 1 placed on a Buchner funnel. Re-extract the residual material with 100 ml of acetone. Follow steps as in 4.4.1 after concentration to oily layer.
NOTE 1 -As the extraction and partitioning procedures are based on fat, moisture, and sugar content of the food material, refer food composition tables for these values given in The .Nutrition Value of Indian Foods and Planning of Sati.ffactory D& by W. R. Aykrod, ICMR, New Delhi or equivalent.

N OTE 2 -Where sample extracts pose difficulty in filteration or thick emulsions are formed during partitioning, centrifugation of the material at ahout 3 000 r/min for about 10 minutes can be resorted to.

4.5 Clean Up 4.5.1 The partitioned extracts obtained in 4.3.1 to 4.3.3 are suitable for direct estimation by alkali flame ionization detector up to 0.1 bg/g level. However, for extracts from 4.4.1 to 4.4.4 and estimations below 0.1 fig/g level of the residues and/or estimation by electron capture detector, further clean up by column chromatography is necessary.
4.5.2 Prepare the chromatographic column by packing with 1 cm layer of glass wool at the bottom followed by 10 cm layer of florisil and 1 cm layer of anhydrous sodium sulphate. Prewash this column with 100 ml of benzene and discard eluate. Dissolve residues in the concentrator tube/flask in two 5 ml portions of benzene and transfer to the column bed. Open the stopcock and allow the column to run till the transferred material soaks into the absorbent. Close the stopcock and fill the column with 200 ml of elutant, benzene-ethyl acetate solution (95 : 5 u/v). Collect in a round bottomed flask. Concentrate eluate in a rotary vacuum evaporator on water bath at temperature of 45�C. Transfer quantitatively to a graduated test tube with acetone and make to suitable volume for analysis. 4.5.3 Calibrate the Aorisil column by eluting standard solution of ( 1 @g/ml ) phosalone with the elutant. 5. GAS CHROMATOGRAPHK

DETERMINATION

5.1 Principle - Phosalone residues obtained after sample extraction and partitioning are measured by gas chromatograph equipped with alkali flame ionization detector (AFID) Q uantitation by gas chromatograph equipped w i t h e l e c t r o n c a p t u r e d e t e c t o r ( E C D ) r e q u i r e f u r t h e r clean-up by column chromatography. The amount of residues is determined by comparing the response with the response for a known standard of similar concentration. 5.2 Apparatus 5.2.1 Gas Chromatograph - A gas chromatograph equipped with thermoionic detector operated under the following suggested parameters. These parameters may be varied as per available facilities provided standardization is done:

5.3.1 Reference Standard of Phosalone ( High Purity ) 5.3.2 Prepare working standard solution of phosalone in acetone of l.OtLg/nrl b y a p p r o p r i a t e dilution of a more concentrated stock solution. 5.4 Procedure 5.4.1 Alkali Flame Ionization Detector ( AND) - Inject a range of duplicate volumes ( 2 to 5 ~1 ) of the working standard solution into the column. Measure peak response as peak height/area. Calculate mass of pure phosalone from the volume of standard solutions injected. Now inject known volume ( 2 to 5 ~1) of the sa.mple extracts made to specific volume after partitioning/clean up. Measure the peak response of the sample at the specific retention time of the standard phosalone.

8

IS : 11301 - 1985 5.4.2 Electron Capture Detector ( ECD ), - Inject a volume of ( 2 to 8 ~1) of the working standard solution into the column. Measure peak response as height/area and calculate mass of phosalone from the volume injected. After standardization, inject known volume ( 2 to 8 ~1 ) of the sample, extract after clean up and made to specific volume. Measure peak response of the sample at specific retention time of the phosalone standard. 5.5 Calculations Phosalone residues, lJg/g ( ppm ) = where A i = peak height/area of the sample;
